external_entities.name: user's browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser that communicates with the web application from outside the system's network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application serving browser traffic and placing jobs onto the message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application runs in our web tier.

processes.name: background worker process
processes.description: A background process that picks up jobs and performs the heavy work.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue receiving jobs from the web application for processing by the background worker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker and used to keep application log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The database is also where we keep the application's log records.
data_stores.notes: The text does not specify whether anything is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: A configuration store from which the web application reads its settings, including queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: A configuration store from which the worker reads its settings, including database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: web request
data_flows.description: The user's browser communicates with the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: enqueue jobs
data_flows.description: The web application places jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_flows.notes: The text does not say how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: pick up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_flows.name: read and write database
data_flows.description: The background worker reads from and writes to the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.notes: The text does not say how the worker authenticates to the database.

data_flows.name: read configuration
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from the web application config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: read configuration
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings from the worker config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: and the worker has a worker config.

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet, outside the system's network, through which the browser communicates with the web application.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: over HTTP/S across the public internet

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The network tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The backend network tier containing the message queue, background worker, and database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because a user's browser communicates with it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The description says that a user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker presents a non-web interface because it is described as a background worker process rather than a web application.
assumptions.basis: The process is described as a background worker that picks up jobs and does work.

assumptions.assumption: The user's browser is an external system.
assumptions.basis: The browser is outside the system's network and communicates with the web application.

assumptions.assumption: The public internet, web tier, and backend tier are network trust boundaries.
assumptions.basis: The description distinguishes the public internet as a network location outside the system's network.

assumptions.assumption: The web tier is a network trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The description places the web application in a named web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The backend tier is a network trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The description places the queue, worker, and database in a named backend tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config is confidential because it holds queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The description says the web application config holds the web application's queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config is confidential because it holds database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The description says the worker config holds the worker's database credentials.
